overview: Colorectal cancer affects the colon or rectum and is one of the most common cancers worldwide, causing severe illness and premature death, particularly when diagnosed at advanced stages. The risk of colorectal cancer increases with age, with most cases occurring in people over 50 years. Common symptoms include diarrhoea or constipation, blood in the stool, abdominal pain, unexplained weight loss, fatigue and low iron levels.
symptoms: iron deficiency anaemia due to chronic bleeding
abdominal pain that won’t go away
diagnosis: examination of the inside of the colon using colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy
taking a sample of tissue (biopsy) for histopathology examination
molecular testing to identify specific genetic mutations or biomarkers
prevention: eating a healthy diet rich in fruits and vegetables
avoiding exposure to environmental risk factors
risk_factors: diets high in processed and red meat and low in fruits and vegetables
previous colorectal cancer or certain types of polyps
key_facts: It is the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide
